w10_P4_000740: A conveyor test launches a carton of 15000 grams along the rollers, and the carton's launch speed in metres per second is 2 times the sum of 4 and 3. The bench records the energy the carton carries because of its motion, subtracts a friction allowance of 28 J, and then adds a calibration offset of 12 J. The result is multiplied by 10, because 10 cartons go out in a batch, and a standing allowance of 13 J is added to the batch total. The roller bed is 8 m long, a dimension the bench never uses. What number, in joules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000745: A teaching bench releases a trolley of 56 kg along a level rail. The trolley's release speed in metres per second is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 9x + 18 = 0. The bench records the energy the trolley carries because of its motion and expresses that record in kilojoules. The converted figure is multiplied by 7 for the 7 releases in a demonstration, a standing allowance of 12 kJ is added, and a contractual credit of 17 kJ is then subtracted. The rail stands 1 m above the floor, a height the bench never uses. What value, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000748: A press slide carries a tool of 30000 grams, and the tool's position in metres is modelled by the fitted curve 1x^3 + 1x^2, with x the time in seconds. The rate at which that fitted position curve is changing at the instant x = 1 second gives a base value, and multiplying it by 11 for the eleven-stage linkage gives the acceleration in metres per second squared. The controller works out the force needed for that acceleration, adds a die preload of 15 N, and expresses the result in kilonewtons. A contractual credit of 5 kN is then subtracted. The slide is 2 m long, a dimension the controller never uses. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?
w10_P4_000751: A workshop counts 256 rivets in one bin and 181 in another, and the technician works out the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. He multiplies that number by 8 for the eight channels of his rig, then by 5 for the five-stage booster, and the result is the launch speed in metres per second of a slug of 10000 grams. The bench records the energy the slug holds because of its motion and adds a fixed instrument offset of 19 J. The total is then expressed in kilojoules. What value, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000755: A laboratory holds 180 steel discs of one size and 191 of another, and the demonstrator works out the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. A glider of 26 kg is released along the air track at a speed, in metres per second, equal to that number. The bench records the energy the glider carries because of its motion, then subtracts a friction allowance of 10 J, a bearing allowance of 29 J, and a drag allowance of 9 J in turn. What remains is multiplied by 6, because 6 benches report together. The track is 2 m long, a dimension never used here. What number, in joules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000757: A machine tool drives a head of 64000 grams along its slide, and the head's position in metres is modelled by the fitted curve 2x^3 + 6x^2, with x the time in seconds. The acceleration in metres per second squared is the rate at which the slope of that fitted curve is itself changing at the instant x = 4 seconds. The controller works out the force needed for that acceleration and expresses it in kilonewtons. It multiplies the converted figure by 4 for the 4 heads on the machine, and then by 4 again for the 4 machines in the shop. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?
w10_P4_000763: A plant figure is 3 times an adjusted reading, because 3 lines run together. The adjusted reading is a converted force with a contractual credit of 4 kN subtracted from it. That converted force is the kilonewton form of the force needed to drive a slide of 19 kg, with a bearing preload of 9 N added before the conversion. The slide's acceleration in metres per second squared is what the rate curve 4t^2 + 1t accumulates between t = 0 seconds and t = 2 seconds, starting from zero, with t the time in seconds. What is the plant figure, in kilonewtons?
w10_P4_000765: A workshop ledger closes with a number in kilonewtons, converted from a bench figure. That bench figure is what remains after a mounting tare of 12 N and then a frame tare of 11 N are taken from a reading, and that reading was a bearing preload of 24 N added to the force needed to accelerate a carrier of 72 kg. The carrier's acceleration in metres per second squared is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 9x + 8 = 0. The bench is 1.7 m wide, a dimension the ledger never uses. What number, in kilonewtons, closes the ledger?
w10_P4_000766: A press-shop total is 2 times a hall figure, because two halls report together, and each hall figure is 11 times a line value. Each line value is itself 2 times a converted single-press reading, since two presses share a line. That converted reading is the kilonewton form of the force needed to drive a ram of 134000 grams, and the ram's acceleration in metres per second squared is what the rate curve 1t^2 + 7t accumulates between t = 3 seconds and t = 4 seconds, starting from zero at t = 3 seconds, with t the time in seconds. What is the press-shop total, in kilonewtons?
w10_P4_000767: A press line drives a tool of 14000 grams, and the tool's acceleration in metres per second squared is what the rate curve 3t^2 + 2t accumulates between t = 1 second and t = 3 seconds, starting from zero at t = 1 second, with t the time in seconds. The controller works out the force needed to drive the tool and multiplies it by 4 for the 4 tools on a press, by 9 for the 9 presses on the line, and by 12 for the 12 lines in the plant. What figure, in newtons, does the controller report?
w10_P4_000770: A rolling mill drives a carrier of 56000 grams along its bed. The rate at which the carrier's acceleration builds, in metres per second cubed, follows 2t^2 + 6t, and between t = 2 seconds and t = 4 seconds the acceleration accumulates from zero at the start of that interval, giving the acceleration the mill uses. From the force needed to drive the carrier the controller subtracts a bearing tare of 22 N, then adds a mounting allowance of 15 N, and finally adds a further rigging allowance of 5 N. What figure, in newtons, does the controller report?
w10_P4_000776: A conveyor drive accelerates a crate of 127000 grams along the rollers, and the acceleration in metres per second squared is the sum of the whole numbers from 1 to 11. The controller works out the force needed for one push and multiplies it by 6, because 6 pushers act together. The total is expressed in kilonewtons, and a fixed frame allowance of 12 kN is added. The roller bed is 10 m long, a dimension the controller never uses. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?
w10_P4_000781: A test-bed report ends with a number that is 3 times a converted total, because 3 halls report together. That converted total is the kilonewton form of a figure that is 2 times a rig value, and each rig value is 8 times the force needed to drive one slide. Each slide has a mass of 86 kg, and its acceleration in metres per second squared is what the rate curve 2t^2 + 2t accumulates between t = 0 seconds and t = 3 seconds, starting from zero, with t the time in seconds. The hall is 50 m long, a dimension the report never uses. What number, in kilonewtons, ends the report?
w10_P4_000791: A haulage ledger closes with a number found by taking a contractual credit of 14 kN off a figure that was itself a rigging allowance of 20 kN added to a converted reading. That converted reading is the kilonewton form of the force needed to accelerate a wagon of 114 kg. The wagon's acceleration in metres per second squared is 5 times the sum of 3 and 5, with a slip loss of 11 subtracted from that product. The siding is 70 m long, a distance the ledger never uses. What number, in kilonewtons, closes the ledger?
w10_P4_000801: A drone workshop fits the curve 4x^3 - 6x^2 to a flight trace, with x the elapsed time in seconds, and the rate at which that fitted curve is changing at the instant x = 3 seconds gives, in metres per second, the speed of a payload of 22000 grams. The workshop records the energy the payload carries because of its motion and multiplies it by 9, because 9 payloads fly the same profile. A calibration offset of 8 J is added and a handling allowance of 13 J is then subtracted, and the result is expressed in kilojoules. The drone's rotors span 1.4 m, a dimension the workshop never uses. What value, in kilojoules, does the workshop report?
w10_P4_000805: A test facility publishes a number that is 6 times a site figure, because 6 sites report together. Each site figure is a converted total with a contractual credit of 24 kJ subtracted from it, and that converted total is the kilojoule form of a value that is 5 times the energy of a single run. In one run a sled of 44000 grams reaches a speed, in metres per second, equal to what the rate curve 5t^2 + 0t accumulates between t = 2 seconds and t = 3 seconds starting from zero at t = 2 seconds, with t the time in seconds; the energy of the run is the energy the sled carries because of its motion at that speed. What number, in kilojoules, does the facility publish?
w10_P4_000808: A stores clerk counts 398 pins of one type and 283 of another, and works out the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. A slider of 16000 grams is launched along the bench at a speed, in metres per second, equal to that number. The bench records the energy the slider holds because of its motion and adds a fixed instrument offset of 2 J. The result is multiplied by 5 for the 5 launches in a set and by 2 for the 2 sets in the session, and a contractual credit of 20 J is subtracted at the end. What number, in joules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000809: A shunting yard accelerates a wagon of 140000 grams, and the rate at which its acceleration builds, in metres per second cubed, follows 1t^2 + 8t. Between t = 0 seconds and t = 2 seconds the acceleration accumulates from zero, and the value reached at t = 2 seconds is the one used. The controller works out the force needed to accelerate the wagon and expresses it in kilonewtons. It multiplies that converted figure by 4 for the 4 wagons in a rake, by 8 for the 8 rakes in a shift, and by 12 for the 12 shifts in the cycle. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the controller report for the cycle?
w10_P4_000814: A depot report ends with a number that is 4 times a converted reading, because 4 depots report together. That converted reading is the kilonewton form of a figure that is 2 times a bench value, since two tugs work each depot. The bench value is what remains after a rope tare of 21 N is taken from the force needed to accelerate a pallet of 6000 grams, and the pallet's acceleration in metres per second squared is 7 times the sum of 2 and 4. What number, in kilonewtons, ends the report?
w10_P4_000817: A warehouse tug accelerates a pallet of 42 kg across a smooth floor. The acceleration in metres per second squared is 11 times the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 9x + 20 = 0. The controller works out the force needed for the pull, subtracts a rope tare of 2 N, and expresses the remainder in kilonewtons. A contractual credit of 28 kN is then subtracted from the converted figure. The pallet is stacked 1.9 m high, a figure the controller never uses. What number, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?
w10_P4_000824: A launch bench brings a carriage of 55000 grams up to speed along a level rail, and the carriage's acceleration in metres per second squared follows 5t^2 + 5t between t = 0 seconds and t = 2 seconds, starting from rest, with t the time in seconds. The bench records the energy the carriage carries because of its motion at the end of that interval and expresses it in kilojoules. The converted figure is multiplied by 7 for the 7 launches in a programme, a standing instrument allowance of 16 kJ is added, and a further ground-station allowance of 14 kJ is added after that. What figure, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000825: A shaker bench fits the curve 5x^3 - 4x^2 to a recorded trace, with x the time in seconds. At the instant x = 2 seconds the rate at which the slope of that fitted curve is itself changing gives, in metres per second, the speed of a test mass of 31000 grams on the head. The bench records the energy the mass carries because of its motion and expresses that record in kilojoules. The converted figure is multiplied by 12, because 12 benches report together, and a fixed calibration offset of 23 kJ is added at the end. What value, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000826: A depot report ends with a number that is 11 times a yard figure, because 11 yards report together. Each yard figure is a converted reading with a rigging allowance of 20 kN added and a handling credit of 11 kN then subtracted. That converted reading is the kilonewton form of the force needed to accelerate a load of 140000 grams, and the load's acceleration in metres per second squared is the largest whole number that divides both 371 and 360 exactly, with nothing left over. What number, in kilonewtons, ends the report?
w10_P4_000832: A laboratory has 46 brass weights and 14 steel weights, and the demonstrator works out the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. A carrier of 39 kg is launched along the bench rail at a speed, in metres per second, equal to that number. The bench records the energy the carrier holds because of its motion and adds a fixed instrument offset of 4 J. The result is multiplied by 7 for the 7 launches in a run, a standing allowance of 9 J is added, and the total is multiplied by 9 for the 9 runs in the programme. What number, in joules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000844: A crane-yard report ends with a number that is 8 times a yard figure, because 8 yards report together. Each yard figure is a rigging allowance of 24 kN added to a total that is 12 times a converted reading, since 12 lifts make a cycle. That converted reading is the kilonewton form of the force needed to accelerate a hook load of 132 kg, and the load's acceleration in metres per second squared is the larger of the two values of x for which x^2 - 6x + 5 = 0. What number, in kilonewtons, ends the report?
